title: Submit and operate the serial Cell CI queue
summary: Queue an immutable Cell commit for serial merge, bounded repair, mandatory production signing, exact-source deployment and personal outcome email; inspect, pause, cancel, recover or maintain the installed manager.
use_when: Submit a committed Cell change for the complete unattended delivery lifecycle.
Inspect or wait for a retained CI job, pause or resume queue admission, request cancellation, or reconcile a blocked job through its owning providers.
Initialize, install or operate the shared CI manager, or acquire and release its owner-qualified Nucleus requester maintenance hold.
do_not_use_when: Only local check-only validation, a design discussion, uncommitted edits, another repository, remote publication, or an arbitrary email is requested.

The intended action requires automatic conflict resolution, direct model filesystem writes, concurrent repair loops, a larger repair budget than the retained policy, or bypassing an unresolved execution.
outcome: A pinned committed input receives a retained serial job outcome with separate validation, accepted-source, deployment, and Email-acceptance evidence, or remains paused or blocked with its unresolved operation preserved.

interfaces.label: Select an external work volume after quiescence
Install source manager and matching provider

effects: Initialization records one repository, explicit accepted baseline and policy. Submission pins an input commit and appends a durable FIFO job.

New submissions freeze skip_tests=true by default. --run-tests freezes false. Jobs without this field retain test execution. Required non-test checks still run, and receipts and outcome emails identify skipped tests.

The worker merges in a private worktree, runs brokered CI, applies deterministic fixes when the candidate supports them, invokes read-only Nucleus remediation for remaining failures, creates private candidate commits through Git, and atomically advances refs/ci/accepted after successful validation.

Deterministic fixes reuse the existing strict Clippy invocation's complete, nonconflicting MachineApplicable suggestion groups for tracked files and run the formatter once for selected Cargo packages. The validator prepares one retained patch in a temporary tracked snapshot, without changing the committed candidate, and stops before tests and later product stages when that patch is available. The manager records a private child candidate and validates it against the same base before acceptance. This path invokes no model and consumes no model repair point.
The worker requests deployment of the exact accepted commit and sends a deterministic job-outcome email to Email's fixed personal recipient.
Installation selects manager and provider files and configures the current-user service. Pause, cancellation, recovery and maintenance alter only their declared queue or operation state.

New jobs preflight and freeze the host signing policy. After confined validation, the installed manager prepares and verifies signed production candidates before advancing accepted history, even when tests are skipped. Deployment receives the frozen signing selection.
authority: The manager owns serial delivery policy and retained job results; it does not decide provider execution, CI gate success, installed product health, or final inbox delivery.

Submission grants standing authority for the defined bounded repair, accepted-ref update, selected exact-source deployment and frozen outcome notification. Inspection does not grant submission authority.
Development main and the submitter's worktree remain outside the manager's mutation boundary. Accepted automatic repairs remain in accepted and private candidate history.
success: Successful admission returns a retained job identity for a pinned input; it is not successful validation or deployment.

Successful validation identifies the fixed base, exact candidate and completed required gate scope. New jobs also require a matching production receipt and verified native signatures and declared artifact inventory under the frozen host signing policy before accepted state advances.

Deployment success requires matching coordinator evidence for the exact source and released maintenance. A no-product result is reported as no deployment required. Already-included input creates no fresh deployment.
Email success means provider acceptance of the frozen notification, separately from source acceptance and installation success.
failure_and_recovery: Merge conflicts stop automatic processing. Failed jobs and active cancellation pause new jobs; queued cancellation prevents admission without outcome email. Resume does not clear a blocked or unresolved active operation.

Failed or Git-rejected attempts remain charged to the frozen job budget. Under refund_accepted_patches=true, Git acceptance and a recorded private candidate refund one point before later validation. Quota or maintenance deferral preserves the prepared request identity without another charge; unknown or lost execution still requires recovery.

Unknown or lost model execution, missing child completion evidence, or unresolved deployment maintenance remains blocked. Recovery consults owning providers and never invents a success or silently starts a replacement model attempt.

A completed stopped deployment start fails the job before admission only after the coordinator reports not_found for that exact request. The manager retains the stopped diagnostic and pauses the queue without creating an admitted deployment receipt. Admitted, uncertain or uncorrelated results retain reconciliation and recovery requirements.

After an installation that qualifies for the cancelled validation exception, recover JOB reconciles the retained supervisor result and recognizes cancellation before reading the aggregate validation receipt. A completed validation already recorded in job history can also prove cancellation when no newer validation artifacts exist and its candidate and receipt path match. Missing or mismatched terminal evidence remains blocked. Recovery does not rerun a completed stale validation; installation itself does not complete or validate the job.

Outcome email uses one frozen key and payload for at most two Email invocations, at least five minutes apart and within 23 hours. Unproved acceptance after that boundary blocks continuation without a replacement message.

Missing or unusable signing identity rejects new submission. A changed policy, failed signature or production-preparation failure stops before acceptance without requesting model repair or selecting another signer. Retained jobs without a signing snapshot keep their earlier acceptance path.
privacy: Job state retains private source identities, deterministic fix patches and candidate commits, model requests and final responses, diagnostics, deployment records, and notification payloads. There is no automatic pruning.
The agent can read source, contracts and diagnostics through ordinary shell tools under the Nucleus read-only sandbox. Provider disclosure follows Nucleus's execution boundary.

New deterministic emails lead with the outcome and product or check names, include available failed test names or a short diagnostic, and distinguish validation, deployment, recovery, and cleanup failures. Unknown causes remain explicit. Emails omit job and commit IDs, model names, repair budgets, and local artifact paths. Receipts do not promise installed versions or individual final installation states; messages do not infer them. Previously frozen messages keep their exact bytes and key. Emails do not attach the repository, model reasoning, or full CI transcripts.
does_not_authorize: Submission from discovery, status inspection, or a design discussion alone.
Writing development main, pushing Git history, changing provider credentials, deleting retained state, automatically resolving merge conflicts, or clearing unrelated maintenance owners.
Treating elapsed time, process disappearance, model completion, a CI exit code alone, or Email acceptance as proof of a different owner's success condition.

Changing signing configuration, generating or renewing a certificate, selecting another private key, or substituting an unsigned or ad hoc production artifact as part of submission or automated repair.

consumers.statement: The current user and authorized Cell development callers can submit committed inputs and inspect or operate the one configured host queue.
This is not a multi-user service, a multi-repository scheduler, or a general workflow framework.

preconditions.statement: Production requires one configured external APFS volume with ownership enabled, the recorded UUID and mount path, and at least 2 GiB free before new work. The current user owns the fixed workspace.json selection. Configure only after the previous CI queue and deployment have drained and the manager service has stopped. Configuration refuses a second destination, a live or unsettled legacy manager, and unresolved legacy deployment.

Initialize one Git common repository with an explicitly selected known accepted baseline. Install a matching manager/provider, provide Python 3.11 or newer and the repository gate tools, and start the user service. Resume admission explicitly after initialization or an operator pause.

Model repair requires the selected Bazaar prompt versions and a compatible ready Nucleus. Deployment requires its selected products and coordinator prerequisites. Notification requires the installed Email interface and provider access. Discovery establishes none of these live conditions.

New macOS submissions require the exact configured code-signing certificate and usable private key. Initial signing adoption and explicit identity changes require paused CI with all active and queued jobs settled and no live or unresolved deployment or release-publication operation.

inputs.statement: First initialization accepts repository path, accepted-baseline commit, positive first-tier and escalation repair budgets, and positive model timeout seconds. The legacy luna-attempts and terra-attempts flags set the Terra medium and Sol high limits, respectively. Reinitialization cannot replace repository or policy or move advanced accepted history. Submission accepts a commit, optional same-repository path, request identity and repeated deployment products. The job freezes its resolved input and policy. New submissions freeze refund_accepted_patches=true, so the tier budgets count unrefunded attempts; existing jobs without the flag keep their limit on all invocations.

The agent is asked to return only a raw Git patch in its final response, potentially covering multiple files. The exact final response is retained. The application input gains a missing final LF; git apply --cached --recount --whitespace=nowarn decides acceptance against a private index initialized from the recorded parent. The manager adds no patch grammar, size, byte, path, file-type or changed-content restrictions to Git's rules.
Uncommitted working files are not a submitted candidate. Direct model writes and patch proposals from reasoning, execution logs or another output channel are not supported.

New submissions freeze skip_tests=true by default, or false with --run-tests, plus the normalized host signing_policy. Missing test fields retain test execution; missing signing fields retain the legacy acceptance path. Idempotent request-key retry returns the original signing snapshot rather than adopting changed host configuration.

outputs.statement: Submission returns a durable job identity. Status exposes retained queue or selected-job phase, candidate, attempts, validation, deployment and notification evidence. Each job also exposes derived repair_budget fields mode, total, used, remaining, refunded, and invocations. Mode is refund_accepted or invocations. Total is the sum of tier budgets, used is recorded attempts minus refunds, remaining is available budget, refunded counts candidate-backed refunds permitted by the frozen policy, and invocations counts all retained attempts. Original-policy jobs have zero refunds. Wait observes that same job. Provider receipts remain separate from the manager's job outcome.
A queue receipt is not proof of full-repository CI, deployment, final inbox delivery, or semantic correctness of an automated patch.

New jobs retain production_receipt with exact source commit, signing-policy object, product scope, preparation source/build identities, and signed candidate identities and declared artifact inventory. configuration_error identifies signing selection or key-usability failures; validation and deployment receipts remain distinct.

When deterministic fixes are available, aggregate validation state autofix reports a retained patch before tests and later product stages. The manager records an autofixing phase, patch evidence and private candidate commit. This result is not passing validation; the corrected candidate must complete the required gate scope.

data_semantics.statement: Input Ci is a complete commit including ancestry. Base Bi is accepted when the serial job is claimed. Every repair candidate is committed privately and validated against that fixed Bi. Accepted history can include repairs absent from development main.

Already-included means Ci is an ancestor of accepted history, not that a fresh deployment occurred. A later descendant submission can include an earlier failed change and receives its own frozen repair budget.
Accepted-source, installed-source, job outcome and notification-acceptance are distinct records. A later deployment or email failure does not erase a previously advanced accepted ref.

identity_and_units.statement: Git commit IDs identify input, base and candidate. Manager job IDs and monotonic enqueue sequence identify serial work. Nucleus IDs, deployment request IDs and Email keys correlate separately retained provider operations.

Local created and updated fields and attempt stamps use Unix seconds. Model timeout uses seconds. Under the refund policy, repair limits count unrefunded attempts rather than diagnostics or total invocations. Attempt numbers increase monotonically and provider identities remain unique across refunds; no attempt history is deleted or reused.

The certificate SHA-1 fingerprint selects one signing certificate, not an executable hash algorithm. Cell compares normalized policy objects directly. Stable code identifiers combine the configured namespace, canonical product key, and declared executable key; source version and build path do not enter them.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: Status reads retained manager records for the configured queue or one requested job at read time. Those records contain the last observed provider evidence; status does not turn them into live provider probes. Validation receipts enumerate required scope and completed gate receipts.
No maximum queue delay, provider-observation age, completion deadline, comprehensive source-correctness claim or final inbox-observation guarantee is supplied.

access.statement: The supported surface is the current-user cell-ci CLI, root and product ci.sh manager wrappers, and installed worker. Bare wrapper invocations and direct validation flags are unsupported. Product wrappers do not restrict coverage. The manager invokes the internal committed-range validator; older workers must be updated before submitting manager-only wrapper commits. Production state is one private host directory and configured Git common repository. Linked worktrees share that identity.

Nucleus jobs use requester program ci-manager, workspaceAccess read-only, ordinary local shell execution enabled and web search disabled. Only the manager applies final-response patches and performs Git, deployment and notification mutations.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: The external workspace holds manager, broker and deployment journals, worktrees, diagnostics, Cargo downloads, compiler outputs, release bundles, tool caches and temporary files. CI bodies and release compiler processes run under the macOS filesystem sandbox with writes confined to this workspace plus /dev/null and /dev/tty. Source Git metadata, installed programs, service configuration, credentials and live provider state remain host-owned. Nucleus runtime records keep their separate provider retention.

FIFO submission records survive caller exit. The singleton worker keeps one active lifecycle through merge, checks, repair, acceptance, deployment and notification; it reconciles retained effects after interruption before claiming later work.

Private input and candidate refs retain submitted and repaired history. Compare-and-swap advances accepted only from the captured base to the validated candidate. Model requests and external operation identities are saved before effects. A persisted private candidate records Git acceptance and establishes one refund under the frozen refund policy, independently of later CI success. Refunds preserve earlier failed-attempt charges for the whole job.

The validator captures suggestions during its existing strict Clippy invocation. It applies only complete, nonconflicting MachineApplicable groups for tracked files in a temporary snapshot, then runs the formatter once for the selected packages. It preserves the clean committed candidate throughout brokered checks. The manager retains the resulting raw patch, applies it through a private index and records a private child candidate before revalidation. The next validation recomputes source selection against the fixed base. Remaining failures enter the existing bounded model path after revalidation.

Pause stops new admission without erasing active work. Cancellation drains active effects; queued cancellation prevents admission without email. Nucleus-only owner-qualified maintenance blocks new repair admission and releases only its own hold; it does not clear operator pause or unresolved work.

A completed stopped deployment start fails before admission only after a coordinator status read reports not_found for the same request. The manager retains the stopped diagnostic and pauses the queue without creating an admitted deployment receipt. Admitted, uncertain or uncorrelated evidence retains the existing reconciliation and recovery requirements.

Installation normally requires paused admission and no active job. Service stop always requires both conditions. Installation selects immutable program and matching provider bytes, refuses foreign owned paths, and attempts restoration on failure. After stopping its owned service during installation or rollback, the installer waits up to 10 seconds for the worker lock, refuses to proceed if it remains held, and retains all required checks under the lock after acquisition. The repository wrapper always runs init and install from source and dispatches other manager commands to the installed cell-ci; an installed install command selects its own release bytes.

Installation alone permits one explicitly cancelled active job blocked in checking when admission is paused, the job has no pending recovery request, accepted source, model attempts, unresolved model execution or deployment, and its exact retained validation supervisor request and matching result prove that the process exited. The installer verifies these conditions before stopping its owned service and again under the worker lock. It preserves the job and evidence without marking success. Missing process completion evidence and other blocked jobs do not qualify. Supported recover under the new worker handles cancellation through the ordinary outcome path.

For new jobs, confined passing validation enters a supervised preparing phase using signing and build modules pinned in the installed manager release. It prepares checked plus explicitly requested deployment products, verifies cached and final candidates under the frozen policy, retains the production receipt, and rechecks signatures and policy before accepted-ref compare-and-swap. Tests may be skipped, but this phase may not. Signing failures never enter automated repair. The Keychain retains the key; the manager supplies repair agents no private-key material or signing configuration writer.

operational_limits.statement: New-job defaults are three unrefunded gpt-5.6-terra medium attempts followed by one unrefunded gpt-5.6-sol high attempt, with a 600-second model execution timeout. The next tier follows the unrefunded count, so accepted patches can continue beyond four total invocations; no separate total-invocation ceiling applies. This budget bounds unrefunded points, not total work, runtime, or cost. Nucleus owns capacity and quota waiting. Git owns patch acceptance; the manager imposes no additional patch limits.

Deterministic fix application invokes no model and consumes no model repair point. Suggestions that are not MachineApplicable, incomplete groups and conflicting groups are omitted. Applying a patch is not proof that the lint is resolved or that the change is semantically correct; the corrected candidate requires validation.

Notification permits two Email process invocations using the same frozen message and key, at least 300 seconds apart and before 82800 seconds from notice creation. Email owns its separate internal transport retry limit.

Concurrent automated repair loops, automatic merge-conflict repair, direct model patch application, manager self-deployment, automatic artifact pruning, and blind retry of unresolved provider work are not supported.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Manager release 0.7.0 uses journal schema 1, queue contract 9, committed-range aggregate CI receipt schema 1, production receipt schema 1, signing policy schema 1, and the declared dependency bounds. Installation preserves all frozen job policies. Retained jobs without signing_policy do not gain a signing phase; jobs without the refund or test flags preserve their earlier behavior. Drain legacy work before signing adoption or rotation.

The installed manager enables the optional internal --autofix-patch mode only when the committed candidate contains pipeline/autofix.py. Older candidates retain check-only validation. The additive mode uses aggregate state autofix and retained fix history within schema 1; it does not change frozen model, test or signing policy. Updating a checkout does not replace the running worker. Pause and drain the manager before installing the matching program and provider.
No automatic journal migration, rollback across incompatible state, cross-release support window or deprecation interval is promised.

The manager supports Nucleus requester contracts 2 and 3 for its unchanged HTTP execution, replay, cancellation, and quota integration. It uses no requester backup facility. Explicit Bazaar JSON selection supports read contracts 1 and 2 during the manager-before-product cutover.

reliances.statement: Read-only agent execution, immutable submission identity, cancellation and quota behavior rely on the Nucleus requester contract; Nucleus does not decide whether a patch fixes CI.
Authored repair instructions and prompt templates rely on exact versioned Bazaar reads. Missing prompt state does not permit a hard-coded fallback.
The final notification relies on Email's fixed-recipient, stable-key submission and acceptance receipt. Inbox delivery remains outside manager success.

Commit reachability, merge results, patch acceptance and application, private worktrees and atomic accepted-ref updates rely on Git. No dedicated installed Chancery contract describes this dependency.
Candidate coverage and gate evidence rely on Cell's committed-range CI dispatcher and host broker. These remain independently authoritative and have no dedicated installed Chancery contract.
Exact-source installation and maintenance recovery rely on the Cell deployment coordinator and selected product installers; no dedicated coordinator Chancery contract is installed.
The macOS user service relies on launchd supervision, while the manager retains domain state and singleton ownership.

Exact macOS certificate selection, private-key readiness, stable code identifiers, and explicit configuration changes rely on the shared Cell signing contract. This does not grant another product signing-configuration authority.
